claims.text: Equimolar HEAs with significant atomic-size mismatch exhibit pronounced lattice distortion.
The unusual combination of strength and ductility under dynamic loading is caused by heterogeneous local stress fields associated with severe lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation glide and thereby raises strength.
Lattice distortion promotes dynamic recovery through reversible dislocation cross-slip, sustaining ductility.
A conventional alloy with lower configurational entropy will consequently have less lattice distortion.
Local heterogeneous stress fields arising from atomic-size mismatch modulate dislocation interactions.
The random distribution of multiple elements creates a spectrum of local yield thresholds.
Local lattice fields hinder uniform dislocation motion and preserve strength under dynamic loading.
Local lattice fields enable localized cross-slip and recovery processes that preserve ductility.
The combination of impeded dislocation motion and localized recovery produces a superior strength–ductility trade-off.
The HEA will have a higher work-hardening rate than the conventional-alloy baseline during dynamic tests.
The HEA will have more stable flow stress than the conventional-alloy baseline during dynamic tests.
The HEA will exhibit delayed strain localization relative to the conventional-alloy baseline.
The HEA will exhibit greater uniform elongation than the conventional-alloy baseline during dynamic tests.
The proposed mechanism operates from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures when the strain rate activates dislocation mechanisms.
The mechanism should be evident specifically in single-phase HEAs with significant atomic-size differences.
The mechanism may not apply to multiphase or nanoprecipitate-containing HEAs because those structures introduce competing strengthening mechanisms.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can provide an alternative strength–ductility mechanism through dislocation transmission and relief of stress concentrations.
The relative importance of lattice distortion and other deformation mechanisms may depend on temperature and strain rate.
The lower-entropy baseline lacks the heterogeneous local stress-field distribution attributed to the HEA.
